Network Access Control - NAC
item.description: They support access management by enforcing organizational policies regarding the people and devices that are attempting to access the network. NAC systems allow cybersecurity professionals to monitor the users and devices that are attached to the network, and manually control access as required. Network access control systems provide the following capabilities: Rapidly enforcing access policies that have been created for different operational conditions. Recognizing and profiling connected users and devices to prevent malicious software on non-compliant systems from causing damage. Providing secure access to network guests, often through registration portals. Evaluating device compliance with security policies by user type, device type, and operating system prior to permitting network access. Mitigating security incidents by blocking, isolating, or repairing non-compliant devices. non-compliant: required updates personal devices IoT BYOD This heavily plays into bring your own device programs, public wifi, and IoT. Because BYOD and loT networking greatly expand the network attack surface, NAC system automation features make focused control of network access by such devices practical. The NAC system is configured to enforce organizational policies. The relevant policies are enacted to permit or deny network access according to a wide range of factors that the NAC system detects on the devices that are attempting access. Without NAC systems it would be impossible for cybersecurity personnel to evaluate the thousands of devices that could attempt to access the network. NAC is an important component of a zero-trust security architecture that enforces security policy compliance with all devices and users that attempt to access the network. Summary Use #principle_of_Least_Privaledge with all devices. network separation between IoT, BYOD, guest, and internal devices.

Access Controlls
item.description: Logical Controls Administrative Controls Authentication, Authorization, Accounting Federated Identity Management (aka Single Sign-On - SSO) MFA NAC Logical access controls are the hardware and software solutions used to manage access to resources and systems. These technology-based solutions include tools and protocols that computer systems use for identification, authentication, authorization, and accountability. Encryption is the process of taking plaintext and creating ciphertext. Smart cards have an embedded microchip. Passwords are protected strings of characters. Biometrics are users' physical characteristics. Access control lists (ACLs) define the type of traffic allowed on a network. Protocols are sets of rules that govern the exchange of data between devices. Firewalls prevent unwanted network traffic. Routers connect at least two networks. Intrusion detection systems monitor a network for suspicious activities. Clipping levels are certain allowed thresholds for errors before triggering a red flag. This is where policies and procedures come in Administrative access controls are the policies and procedures defined by organizations to implement and enforce all aspects of controlling unauthorized access. Administrative controls focus on personnel and business practices. Policies are statements of intent. Procedures are the detailed steps required to perform an activity. Hiring practices define the steps an organization takes to find qualified employees. Background checks are a type of employee screening that includes information of past employment verification, credit history, and criminal history. Data classification categorizes data based on its sensitivity. Security training educates employees about the security policies at an organization. Reviews evaluate an employee's job performance. The concept of administrative access controls involves three security services: authentication, authorization, and accounting (AAA). These services provide the primary framework to control access, preventing unauthorized access to a computer, network, database, or other data resource. It verifies the identity of each user, to prevent unauthorized access. Users prove their identity with a username or ID. In addition, users need to verify their identity by providing one of the following: Something they know (such as a password) Something they have (such as a token or card) Something they are (such as a fingerprint) In the case of two factor authentication, which is increasingly becoming the norm, the system requires a combination of two of the above rather than just one to verify someone's identity. It determines which resources users can access, along with the operations that users can perform. Some systems accomplish this by using an access control list, or an ACL. An ACL determines whether a user has certain access privileges once the user authenticates. It can also control when a user has access to a specific resource. It keeps track of what users do - including what they access, the amount of time they access resources, and any changes they make. Cybersecurity accounting services track each data transaction and provide auditing results. System administrators can set up computer policies to enable system auditing. Cybersecurity accounting tracks and monitors in real time. The concept of AAA is like using a credit card that identifies who can use it, how much that user can spend, and accounts for items or services the user purchased.

Hypervisor architecture
item.description:
Hyper-V is a Type 1 Hypervisor "Bare Metal Hypervisor" Installed Directly on the Physical Host Direct access to the physical resources of the physical host Hypervisors have drivers to be able to communicate with those resources There are 2 "Architectures" or flavors of Type 1 Hypervisors where those drivers are stored: Monolithic Microkernelized Drivers exist within the hypervisor Very good performance! Larger Hypervisor However, all drivers are shared, limiting hardware support because the driver is specifically made for the Hypervisor! Small compatibility list of drivers Drivers exist within the Management Partition (AKA the Parent Partition) Smaller Hypervisor a little bit slower more secure due to individual drivers for each VM. All Windows drivers created from various vendors for their hardware can still be used and run in the Management Partition The Guest VM's have their own Child Partitions for virtual drivers. The Child Partitions do not impact the security of the Parent Partitions. biggest issue is if the drivers in the parent go then so do the children.
REVIEW OF DRIVERS Drivers are software programs that facilitate communication between hardware devices and the operating system of a computer. They serve as a bridge that allows the operating system to interact with and control the hardware components of a computer Drivers are essential for enabling the operating system to recognize, configure, and utilize hardware devices efficiently. There are drivers for CPU, Memory, Display, Storage, Network Cards, etc.

item.description:
Network scanning goals Scanning tools - Nmap overview Review TCP vs UDP and TCP three-way handshake Overview of common network scanning types Banner grabbing and OS fingerprinting Network scanning actively probes systems and networks to discover technical information about a target. It builds on reconnaissance by moving from broad information gathering to direct observation of hosts and services. Scanning results help identify systems and services that may deserve closer investigation. Because scanning creates network traffic, it should be performed only within an authorized scope. Note this is where we cross over from passive to active reconassance Identify live hosts on the network Discover open, closed, or filtered ports Identify services running on reachable ports Collect clues about service versions and operating systems Understand parts of the target network and exposed attack surface Use the findings to focus later enumeration and vulnerability assessment

. Host discovery asks which systems appear to be reachable before spending time scanning individual ports. . ICMP echo requests ("ping") are one possible discovery method. . A response can indicate that a host is reachable. . No response does not prove that a host is offline - firewalls or hosts may block or ignore ICMP. . Scanning tools can use additional discovery techniques when ICMP is unavailable.


Banner grabbing collects information that a network service reveals about itself. A banner may provide clues such as the service/application name, software version, server type, or protocol information. This information can help connect an open port to a specific product or technology. Service and version information can then be researched for configuration issues or known vulnerabilities. Banners are clues rather than proof - they can be changed, hidden, or misleading.

Ethical hacking
item.description: An ethical hacker uses hacking knowledge and techniques, which is the same as those used by malicious hacker, with authorization to identify vulnerabilities and improve security. Activities may include vulnerability research and assessment, penetration testing, network testing, web application testing and wireless testing. Ethical hackers may also assess human and procedural weaknesses when explicitly authorized. The technical skills can overlap with malicious hacking. However, authorization, scope, intent and professional conduct make the difference. The main difference Ethical hackers have permission to hack an organization and only go where they have permission to go within that organization. Ethical hacking can discover vulnerabilities before malicious attackers exploit them. It helps validate security controls and identify configuration mistakes. It can demonstrate realistic attack paths and help organizations prioritize remediation. It also supports security improvement, incident preparedness and compliance activities. Golden rule: never test a system unless you have permission. Obtain clear authorization and understand the agreed scope. Stay within scope and minimize unnecessary impact or damage. Protect confidential information discovered during testing. Document findings accurately and report vulnerabilities responsibly. Never use discovered information or access for personal benefit. item.title: High Availability
item.description: The term 'high availability' describes systems designed to avoid downtime as much as possible. The continuous availability of information systems is imperative, not only to organizations but to modern life, as we are all using and relying on computer and information systems more than ever before. High availability systems typically are based on three design principles: eliminating single points of failure, providing for reliable crossover, and detecting failures as they occur. The first principle that defines high availability systems starts with identifying all system devices and components whose failure would result in system-wide failure. Methods to eliminate single points of failure include replacing or removing hot stand-by devices, redundant components, and multiple connections or pathways. Redundant power supplies, backup power systems and backup communications systems all provide for reliable crossover - the second design principle. The third principle is active device and system monitoring to detect many types of events including system and device failures. Monitoring systems may even trigger the backup system in the case of failure. Every organization wants to be able to operate uninterrupted, even under extreme conditions, such as during an attack.One of the most popular high availability goals is often called 'five nines.' It gets its name from its aim to achieve an availability rate of 99.999%, which is five nines in a row. In practice, this means that downtime is less than 5.26 minutes per year.Common steps taken to reach the five nines include: Standardized Systems Systems standardization provides for systems that use the same components. As a result, parts inventories are easier to maintain and it is possible and easy to swap components, even during an emergency. In highly secure information system facilities, guards control access to the organization's sensitive areas. The benefit of using guards here is that they can adapt more than automated systems. Guards can learn and distinguish many different conditions and situations and make decisions on the spot. Clustering Multiple devices grouped together provide a service that, to users, appears to be a single entity. If one device in a cluster fails, the other devices remain available and can step in. Shared Component Systems Systems are built so that a complete system can stand in for one that failed. N+1 redundancy helps ensure system availability in the event of a component failure. It means that components (N) need to have at least one backup component (+1). A good way to think about this is that a car has four tires (N) and a spare tire (+1) in the trunk in case of a flat. Although a system using N+1 architecture contains redundant equipment, it is not a fully redundant system. My summary Always have at least one extra of what you need always ready for the event that it goes down. N +1 Is specifically not in use/on its own. Like bellow the N+1 is the secondary network, not the redundancy in the first.

item.description:
. A Hypervisor is the software layer on a physical host that coordinates virtual machines. A Hypervisor manages virtual machines and is responsible for allocating resources to each virtual machine. The Hypervisor is ultimately what makes virtualization possible. There are two types of Hypervisor: Type 1 and Type 2 Also known as the "Bare Metal Hypervisor" Type 1 Hypervisor is installed directly on the physical host Has direct access to the physical resources of the physical host which then allocates the available resources to the virtual machines Hypervisor loads (boots) first, before the Operating System Administrators have the ability to create clusters with many Type 1 Hypervisors (but not all) Also known as "Hosted Hypervisor" Type 2 Hypervisor is installed on top of the host Operating System (ie Windows 10) The host Operating System manages the hardware resources The Type 2 Hypervisor requests the resources from the Operating System Type 2 Hypervisors do not support clustering Type 1 Hypervisors have better performance compared to Type 2 Type 1 Hypervisors have direct access to hardware resources! Type 2 Hypervisors need to request resources from the OS first, the OS then accesses the hardware resources Hyper-V is Type 1
Hyper-V is a Type 1 Hypervisor! Can be confusing because on Windows 10 / 11 it's a Feature that's enabled from the Control Panel Can be confusing because on Server 2016/2019/2022 it's enabled as a Server Role Hyper-V Manager "appears" to look like an application, but this is what an administrator uses to create/manage VMs Hyper-V is the Virtual Machine Manager When Creating New VM’s When creating New Server VM’s use datacenter not standard. (ie to an External Hard Drive - SSD) There are 3 Types of Imports when using Hyper-V Manager This type of import allows you to import, or "register," a VM where the files and VHD of the VM are already moved to the host You can perform this import when the files are already moved to the new host (ie VM files are cut and pasted from an SSD to a host computer prior to starting the Import process) This import will maintain the same unique ID this if faster then restore since it doesn't need to move a bunch of files. less work for hyper-v. This type of import allows you to import by copying the files and VHD of the VM are from one location to another This import will copy the VM files to a new host, the original files will remain in-tact on the original source (ie VM files saved on an SSD) The original exported files remain unchanged and can be reused for future imports This import will also maintain the same unique ID of the VM This type of import allows you to create "templates" of VMs This type of import can create multiple instances of the same VM on the same host This import will create a new ID for each VM You will not need to use this type of import for this course!

Private Virtual Switches only establish connectivity between virtual machines within a host There is no external connectivity outside of the host External Virtual Switches connect to a network interface card (NIC) on the host essentially “takes over” that NIC Establishes connectivity between virtual machines and intermediary devices (ie physical router) connected to the host Can also establish connectivity between virtual machines and other physical host
Hypervisors can also provide virtual machines with immediate connectivity to the internet This is known as the "Default Switch" on Windows 11. This is not included with Server! 1 #> param( [ValidateSet("BIOS", "OS", "Service", "LogicalDisk")] [string] $InfoClass = "BIOS", [string] $Device = "LocalHost", [parameter(Mandatory = $false)] [string] $OutFile_Path ) #sets the variable for the type of data being collected if ($InfoClass -eq "BIOS") { $InfoClass_var = "Win32_Bios" } elseif ($InfoClass -eq "OS"){ $InfoClass_var = "Win32_OperatingSystem" } elseif ($InfoClass -eq "Service"){ $InfoClass_var = "Win32_Service" } elseif ($InfoClass -eq "LogicalDisk"){ $InfoClass_var = "Win32_LogicalDisk" } #creates the formatting for the teble and data if ($InfoClass -eq "BIOS"){ $Table_Data = Select-Object -Property SMBIOSBIOSVersion,Name,Version,SerialNumber,Manufacturer } elseif ($InfoClass -eq "OS"){ $Table_Data = Select-Object -Property SystemDirectory,Organization,BuildNumber,SerialNumber,Version } elseif ($InfoClass -eq "Service"){ $Table_Data = Select-Object -Property Name,ProccessID,StartMode,State } elseif ($InfoClass -eq "LogicalDisk"){ $Table_Data = Select-Object -Property DeviceID,@{name='FreeSpace';expression={[Math]::Round($_.FreeSpace / 1MB, 3)}}, @{name='Size';expression={[math]::Round($_.Size / 1GB, 3)}}, @{name='%Free';expression={[Math]::Round($_.FreeSpace / $_.Size * 100, 3)}} } #collects info $Device_Data = Get-WmiObject -Class $InfoClass_var -ComputerName $Device |Select-Object $Table_Data #creates file name and full path $File_Name = "$($Device)-$($InfoClass)-$(Get-Date -Format yyyy-mm-dd).csv" $OutFile_Path_compleate = $OutFile_Path + "\" + $File_Name #creates file if specifyed if ($OutFile_Path) { Get-WmiObject -Class $InfoClass_var -ComputerName $Device |Select-Object $Table_Data |Export-Csv -Path $OutFile_Path_compleate } #prints data to the terminal $Device_Data |Format-Table -AutoSize -Wrap

item.description: #Get-ServiceHealthReport.ps1 #Author: Ryder Fryling #Created: 2026/03/22 #Version 1.0 #Updated: N/A #Description: This script Audits Windows services by status, startup type, and service account. <# .SYNOPSIS Audits Windows services by status, startup type, and service account. .DESCRIPTION Queries Windows services using Get-Service and Get-CimInstance, then filters and reports based on the specified criteria. Useful for identifying stopped auto-start services, services running under non-standard accounts, or summarizing overall service health. .PARAMETER Status Filter services by status. Valid values: Running, Stopped, All. Defaults to All. .PARAMETER StartupType Filter by startup type. Valid values: Automatic, Manual, Disabled, All. Defaults to All. .PARAMETER AccountFilter If specified, shows only services running under this account name (partial match). For example, "LocalSystem" or "Network". .PARAMETER SortBy Property to sort results by. Valid values: Name, Status, StartType. Defaults to Name. .EXAMPLE .\Get-ServiceHealthReport.ps1 Lists all services sorted by name. .EXAMPLE .\Get-ServiceHealthReport.ps1 -Status Stopped -StartupType Automatic Shows only stopped services that are configured to start automatically (potential problems that need attention). .EXAMPLE .\Get-ServiceHealthReport.ps1 -AccountFilter "LocalSystem" -SortBy Status Shows services running as LocalSystem, sorted by their current status. #> param( [validateSet("Running", "Stopped", "All")] [string]$Status = "All", [validateSet("Automatic", "Manual", "Disabled", "Auto", "All")] [string]$StartupType = "All", [Parameter(Mandatory = $False)] [string]$AccountFilter, [validateSet("Name", "Status", "StartType", "StartMode", "State")] [string]$SortBy = "Name" ) #gets the services $services = Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_Service #sorts them by status if ($Status -ne "All") { $services = $services | Where-Object { $_.State -eq $Status } } #sorts them by start type if ($StartupType -ne "All") { $services = $services | Where-Object { $_.StartMode -eq $StartupType } } #filters the accounts to best match user input if ($AccountFilter) { $services = $services | Where-Object { $_.StartName -like "*$AccountFilter*" } } #formats the $SortBy to be valid input options if ($SortBy -eq "Status") { $SortBy = "State" } elseif ($SortBy -eq "StartType") { $SortBy = "StartMode" } #sorts the data then makes the table and formats it $services | Sort-Object -Property $SortBy | ForEach-Object { [PSCustomObject]@{ Name = $_.Name DisplayName = $_.DisplayName Status = $_.State StartType = $_.StartMode Account = $_.StartName } } | Format-Table -Property Name,Status,StartType,Account,DisplayName -AutoSize -Wrap

item.description: #Get-DiskReport.ps1 #Author: Ryder Fryling #Created: 2026/03/19 #Version 1.0 #Updated: N/A #Description: This script reports disk space for one or more drives, with output format controlled by a parameter. <# .SYNOPSIS This script reports disk space for one or more drives .DESCRIPTION This script reports disk space for one or more drives, with output format controlled by a parameter to set the measurment in GB or MB. #> param( [string[]]$driveletter, [Validateset("GB", "MB")] [string]$unit = "GB" ) #formates the user input to match powershell input $DataUnit = if ($unit -eq "GB") { 1GB } else { 1MB } #collects the data Get-Volume -DriveLetter $driveletter | ForEach-Object{ [PSCustomObject]@{ #formates the table with some math Drive = $_.DriveLetter "Total($unit)" = [math]::Round($_.Size / $DataUnit, 2) "Free($unit)" = [math]::Round($_.SizeRemaining / $DataUnit, 2 ) PercentFree = [math]::Round(($_.SizeRemaining / $_.Size) * 100, 2) } }|Format-Table -AutoSize

Before running, verify that your OUs are structured correctly. # # Citations: # ICT 128 Lab 07 - Full lab.pdf - Phase 3 used as reference # defining default password $defaultPass = ConvertTo-SecureString "S@lta5002!" -AsPlainText -Force # importing the csv $userList = Import-Csv -Path (Read-Host "Enter your CSV file's full path") Write-Host "$($userList.Count) users loaded from CSV." # processing CSV users foreach ($user in $userList) { # getting name $fName = $user.'First Name'.Trim() $lName = $user.'Last Name'.Trim() $fullName = "$fName.$lName" # building SAM and UPN $sam = ($fullName -replace '[^a-zA-Z0-9]', '').ToLower() $upn = "$sam@atlas.com" # building path $subDept = $user.Subdepartment $title = $user.Title if ($subDept.Length -gt 5) {$subDept = $subDept.Substring(0, 5)} forEach ($OU in (Get-ADOrganizationalUnit -Filter {Name -like "*"})) { if ($title.Contains("Owner")) { $OUPath = (Get-ADOrganizationalUnit -Filter {Name -eq "Owners"}).DistinguishedName break } elseif ($title.Contains("VP")) { $OUPath = (Get-ADOrganizationalUnit -Filter {Name -eq "VPs"}).DistinguishedName break } elseif ($title.Contains("Operations")) { $OUPath = (Get-ADOrganizationalUnit -Filter {Name -like "Operations*"}).DistinguishedName break } elseif ($title -ceq "CIO") { $OUPath = (Get-ADOrganizationalUnit -Filter {Name -eq "C-Suite"}).DistinguishedName break } elseif ($subDept -eq "Accou") { $OUPath = (Get-ADOrganizationalUnit -Filter {Name -eq "Finance"}).DistinguishedName break } elseif ($SubDept -eq ("Administration")) { $OUPath = (Get-ADOrganizationalUnit -Filter {Name -eq "Administration"}).DistinguishedName break } elseif ($title.Contains("Administrator")) { $OUPath = (Get-ADOrganizationalUnit -Filter {Name -like "IT-Admin*"}).DistinguishedName break } elseif ($title.Contains("Technician")) { $OUPath = (Get-ADOrganizationalUnit -Filter {Name -eq "IT-Staff"}).DistinguishedName break } elseif ($OU.Name.Contains($subDept)) { $OUPath = $OU.DistinguishedName break } } # creating ADuser New-ADUser ` -GivenName $fName ` -Surname $lName ` -Name $fullName ` -DisplayName "$fName $lName" ` -SamAccountName $sam ` -UserPrincipalName $upn ` -Department $user.Department ` -Title $user.Title ` -AccountPassword $defaultPass ` -EmployeeID $user.'Employee ID' ` -Office $user.'Office Location' ` -OfficePhone $user.'Office Local Phone' ` -EmailAddress $upn ` -ChangePasswordAtLogon $true ` -Enabled $true ` -Path "$OUPath" # confirming creation $created = Get-ADUser -Identity $sam -Properties Enabled -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue if ($created){ # if user creation succeeds Write-Host "$sam successfully created (Enabled: $($created.Enabled))" -ForegroundColor Green Write-Host " SubDepartment: $($subDept), OU: $($OUPath)" } else { # item.title: CIM vs WMI vs Native PS CMDlets
item.description: It is a Windows service that exposes hardware, operating system components, and software as structured objects that PowerShell (and other tools) can query. WMI has been built into Windows since Windows 2000. WMI is the windows version of CMI. it is no longer being developed or supported it is being phased out and is not in PS 7 It is a vendor-neutral standard published by the Distributed Management Task Force (DMTF) that defines how system components should be described as objects. WMI is Microsoft's Windows-specific implementation of this standard. the universal version of WMI used to get info about the OS is not available on windows 7 or older you will need to use WMI on those OS's cannot be piped ( | ) Namespaces are the top-level containers. They group related classes together. The most important namespace for network and system administration is root\CIMV2. PowerShell uses this namespace by default when you run Get-CimInstance without specifying one.Other namespaces serve specialised purposes: root\SecurityCenter2: antivirus and firewall product information root\WMI: hardware performance data root\MicrosoftDNS: DNS server management (on DNS servers only) My summery This is like the Directory/folder that the data is located in. Classes define the structure of a type of system component. A class lists all the properties that objects of that type have, along with their data types. Class names follow a convention: Win32_*: provided by the Win32 provider; covers OS, hardware, and networking CIM_*: base classes from the CIM standard; Win32 classes inherit from these __* (double underscore): WMI system classes, metadata about WMI itself My Summery this is the type/format of where the data comes from Instances are the actual data objects, one instance per real component matching the class template. The class Win32_NetworkAdapter defines what properties a network adapter object has; each installed adapter (physical and virtual) is a separate instance of that class.Note Some classes always return exactly one instance (Win32_OperatingSystem) there is only one operating system. Others return many (Win32_NetworkAdapter) one per adapter. Knowing which to expect is part of reading query output correctly.
